newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast holds violence-delayed polls.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast holds violence-delayed polls.

text.p: Ivory Coast wrapped up its second multi-party elections one year late on Sunday with by-elections in areas that saw ethnic and political bloodshed during its 1995 presidential election.

Witnesses said voting began slowly around the opposition Ivorian Popular Front (FPI) stronghold of Gagnoa in the centre west cocoa growing area, where security reinforcements were deployed near polling stations.
Eighteen candidates were contesting eight of the national assembly's 175-seats in the Gagnoa area and in three constituencies in the north and east.
The by-elections will not alter the balance of power in parliament where President Henri Konan Bedie's supporters enjoy a huge majority.

But FPI leader Laurent Gbagbo was trying to regain the seat he held in the previous parliament but was unable to contest in November 1995 because the interior ministry postponed polling around Gagnoa.
The postponement followed clashes between indigenous Bete supporters of Gbabgo's party and migrant farmers of Bedie's Baoule tribe in which 25 people were killed.

Reruns in Seguela in the north and Adzope in the east follow the scrapping of original results. A rerun in Korhogo in the north followed the death of the elected member. Four districts held municipal reruns.
Ivory Coast, the world's top cocoa producer, held its first multi-party elections in 1990.
